title: Runtime contract/version orchestration and non-breaking fallback rules
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Define a pragmatic, operationally-friendly semantic versioning and rollout scheme for the serving runtime that minimizes customer regressions while enabling necessary protocol and ABI changes. This ticket captures the runtime-side contract (headers, behavior tiers), LTS channel rules, staged rollout gates, and the automation/tooling required to help SDKs and on-prem control planes migrate safely. Goals: 1) Make breaking changes explicit and gated. 2) Provide a short-term non-breaking fallback mechanism so clients can opt-in/opt-out per-request. 3) Expose machine-readable compatibility markers for telemetry and migration tooling. 4) Define deprecation windows aligned with LTS channels and explicit upgrade guidance.
acceptance_criteria: A concise runtime semantic versioning table that maps change types to MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH semantics and example change categories
LTS channel definitions with supported upgrade windows and deprecation lifecycles documented (stable, LTS, extended LTS)
Rollout gate spec: canary percentages, health metrics and automatic rollback triggers defined
Compatibility header and deprecation header proposal vetted with SDK teams (string schema + allowed values)
Prototype of a runtime-side 'compatibility adapter' that allows per-request non-breaking fallback behavior and emits telemetry
CLI check (amcli) that warns if a client uses APIs flagged for deprecation and provides migration hints
Documentation page and automated PR template for library teams to opt into or opt-out of strict mode
Integration tests that simulate mixed-version client/agent matrix and validate fallback behavior and KV cache interoperability
decisions: Adopt semver with a runtime-focused interpretation: MAJOR = ABI/protocol break that requires client changes; MINOR = new capabilities/backwards-compatible behavior changes; PATCH = bugfix and performance improvements
Introduce two runtime headers: X-Runtime-Compat (semver token, e.g. 2.1.0) and X-Runtime-Behavior (flags like strict-mode, allow-legacy-keys)
Non-breaking fallback: when behavior changes could affect output, runtime will honor X-Runtime-Behavior=allow-legacy-keys to preserve previous behavior for a bounded grace period
Deprecation window default: MINOR-level deprecation gets 90 days of overlap, MAJOR-level requires migration assistant and 180-day advance notice for hosted customers, longer for Private deployments
LTS channels: stable (rolling, ~30d cadence), LTS (quarterly, 3-month support), extended-LTS (12 months, security/critical fixes only)
Rollout gates: phased canary 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with health checks after each step. Immediate rollback if error-rate or latency delta exceed thresholds (configurable per release).
Telemetry: expose compat_score and migration_events in runtime metrics and link to per-customer migration dashboards
Provide a compat-shim generator for common SDK languages to minimize client-side work when minor contract adaptors are needed
rollout_plan: Phased rollout with automation: 1) Internal canary build with integration tests. 2) Small external canary (1%) against non-critical workloads for 48 hours. 3) Gradual ramp to 5% for 24 hours, then 20% for 24 hours, then 100%. Each stage runs automated checks: latency P50/P95 change, error-rate, token-level regression sample checks. Rollback policy: immediate abort on >2x error-rate or +30% latency P95; manual hold for token-quality regressions. Private deployments receive release notes and must opt-in or schedule upgrade during their 180-day window.
upgrade_tooling: runtime-compat-adapter: a server-side component to support per-request backward-compat flags and to log migration signals
compat-shim-generator: produces lightweight client shims for JavaScript, Python, Go to translate legacy calls to new contract patterns
amcli runtime check: local CLI linter that reads project SDK versions and flags deprecated API usage with migration docs
auto-PR templates in SDK repos that include code snippets and changelog entries for straightforward upgrades
dashboard automation that highlights customers using deprecated features and surfaces migration urgency and suggested next steps
testing_requirements: Matrix tests for client versions [v1.x, v2.{0,1}] interacting with runtime versions [2.0.x, 2.1.x, 3.0.0-canary]
Chaos tests that simulate KV cache miss patterns and verify that fallback flags preserve correctness
Regression suites that run token-delta checks on representative prompts to detect quality drift
End-to-end canary harness that can replay production traffic subsets against canary runtime
Contract fuzzing to detect unexpected header parsing and malformed semver strings
